title: Bounded constructible derived category
statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be a closed symmetric monoidal Grothendieck abelian category whose tensor product is additive, let $X$ be a scheme, and let $\mathcal R$ be a commutative ring object [sk-def-sfb-ring-object] of $\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal A)$ with the sheaf tensor product [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. Write $\Mod_{\mathcal R}$ for its category of module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. A cohomology module is called constructible here in the general ring-object sense of [def-sfb-constructible-module]: there is a finite stratification with immersions $g_a\colon X_a\to X$ such that $\operatorname{mapMod}(g_a^*)(M)$ is locally finitely presented over the pulled-back ring object $g_a^*\mathcal R$ on every stratum, where $M$ denotes the cohomology module.

The bounded constructible derived category
$$
D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal R)\subseteq D(\Mod_{\mathcal R})
$$
is the full subcategory of the ordinary unbounded derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] on those $K$ for which there exist integers $a\le b$ with $H^i(K)=0$ whenever $i<a$ or $i>b$, and every $H^i(K)$ is constructible. Thus its objects are precisely the bounded objects [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories] with constructible cohomology. For two such objects $K,L$ its morphisms, identities and composition are those of $D(\Mod_{\mathcal R})$. No derived completeness condition is imposed.

If the constructible module objects contain zero, are invariant under isomorphism, are closed under kernels and cokernels of morphisms between them, and are closed under extensions, then this full subcategory is triangulated [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory], with the inherited shifts and distinguished triangles.

proof.text: First apply [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-tensor-closed] to the small pro-étale site with the universe and small-skeleton convention of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]: $\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal A)$ is abelian, its sheaf tensor product is additive in each variable, and $\mathcal R\otimes-$ preserves all colimits, hence finite colimits. Thus [lem-sfb-modobj-abelian] applies to the module objects of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and makes $\Mod_{\mathcal R}$ abelian. Its ordinary derived category and cohomology functors are therefore defined by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Define the object predicate by the conjunction of boundedness [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories] and the requirement that every cohomology object $M=H^i(K)$ satisfy [def-sfb-constructible-module]. Apply that definition with the same $\mathcal A$, $X$ and $\mathcal R$: the small site and sheaf tensor are those already fixed, a commutative ring object is in particular a ring object, and each $M$ is a left module object in $\Mod_{\mathcal R}$. For each such $M$, require a finite stratification by immersions $g_a\colon X_a\to X$ for which $\operatorname{mapMod}(g_a^*)(M)$ is locally finitely presented as a module over $g_a^*\mathcal R$. These are precisely the restriction and module transport of that definition; no identification with constant local models or étale-origin modules is used. Boundedness is the vanishing of cohomology outside a finite interval. If initial lower and upper bounds are $a,b$ without $a\le b$, replace them by $\min(a,b),\max(a,b)$; this enlarges the allowed interval and preserves the vanishing assertion. Conversely, vanishing outside $[a,b]$ gives lower bound $a$ and upper bound $b$, hence boundedness. This gives exactly the displayed object predicate.

source.place: ambient abelian module category: lem-sfb-modobj-abelian.md in sk-prop-sfb-module-category; sheaf structure: the existing lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-tensor-closed; object predicate: this definition and Stacks Tag 05RU, label definition-unbounded-derived-category

proof.text: Take the full subcategory on that predicate: its objects are pairs $(K,h_K)$ where $h_K$ is a proof of the predicate, and $\operatorname{Hom}((K,h_K),(L,h_L)):=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\Mod_{\mathcal R})}(K,L)$. Identities and composition are inherited, so the category laws follow from the ambient category laws and the inclusion is fully faithful. Membership asks only for the cohomology conditions in step 1; it asks for no derived completeness datum or property.

source.place: full subcategory; morphisms computed in the ambient derived category; no completeness condition

proof.text: For the corrected triangulatedness assertion, let $\mathcal C=\Mod_{\mathcal R}$ and let $\mathcal B$ be its full subcategory of constructible module objects. The explicit hypotheses give zero, invariance under isomorphism, kernels, cokernels and extensions, exactly the hypotheses of [lem-sbc-cohomology-in-weak-serre-subcategory]. That theorem says that the intersection of $D_{\mathcal B}(\mathcal C)$ with $D^b(\mathcal C)$ is a full triangulated subcategory with inherited shifts and distinguished triangles. An object belongs to this intersection exactly when it satisfies the conjunction in step 1, so it is precisely the full subcategory constructed in step 2. This is an application to the ambient abelian category of module objects, not to étale-origin complexes or to a completed category.

statement_dispute.reason: STATEMENT-DISPUTED: Topological Noetherianity alone does not imply closure of finitely presented coefficient modules under kernels.
statement_dispute.counterexample: Let k be a field, B=k[x,y_1,y_2,\ldots]/(xy_i:i\ge1), X=Spec(\bar k), A=Ab and R the constant sheaf B. Multiplication by x on R has kernel the constant sheaf on (y_i:i\ge1), not finitely generated, hence not locally finitely presented. Its cone has that kernel as H^{-1}, although both source and target are free rank one in degree zero. X is topologically Noetherian.
statement_dispute.correction: Keep the bounded constructible object predicate and full subcategory unchanged in the generic module-object sense. Replace the false unconditional triangulatedness claim by the explicit weak Serre closure criterion of lem-sbc-cohomology-in-weak-serre-subcategory (Stacks 06UQ, 0754), as already corroborated by prop-weil-pbc-module-bounded-constructible-triangulated.

This module publicly retains every original declaration, including the general ring-object predicate, full subcategory, membership characterization and corrected weak Serre triangulatedness statement. It adds their discrete constant-ring presentation on qcqs schemes, where affine-local and finite-global constructible stratifications agree: all integer cohomology modules satisfy the existing affine-local constructibility predicate and vanish outside one ordered finite interval, in the same ordinary standard derived localization. No coefficient size equality, derived completeness or Tor condition is added.
